name: research-thoroughly
query: Research the current state of WebGPU support across the major browsers thoroughly. I need to be sure before we commit to it.
why: The explicit multi-angle request. Decompose into angles, run researchers in parallel up to the ceiling, validate, then synthesize one dated, source-cited brief.

name: is-this-still-true
query: Is it still true that Cloudflare Workers cap CPU time at fifty milliseconds? I read that a while ago and it may have moved.
why: Currency-sensitive claim with an explicit suspicion of staleness. Needs two independent sources, at least one primary, and the date attached.

name: verified-not-guessed
query: What does that API's mid tier actually cost right now? I want a verified number, not a guess.
why: A single fact, but accuracy is the whole point and pricing moves. The inline mode covers quick verified lookups, so the skill still owns it; the full pipeline would be overkill.

name: multi-angle-brief
query: Give me a multi-angle picture of what the EU AI Act obliges a small SaaS company to do.
why: Provider- and project-agnostic by design. A topic spanning several independent domains is exactly what angle decomposition is for, and nothing about it is AI tooling selection.

name: before-building-on-a-moving-fact
query: Before I write this integration, confirm which auth flows their v3 API supports and when v2 gets switched off.
why: Building on a fast-moving fact where being wrong is expensive. A deprecation date is currency-sensitive and needs a primary source.

name: sources-contradict-each-other
query: Everything I read about this contradicts the last thing I read. Can you work out what's actually true?
why: Cross-validation is the phase a single search does not have. Contradictions get flagged by the validator and the brief carries a confidence rating rather than a clean-looking answer.

name: one-line-fact
query: What's the default port for Postgres?
why: A one-line lookup that raw WebSearch answers. Running the pipeline here is the skill's own first anti-pattern.

name: latest-version-lookup
query: What's the latest stable Node version?
why: The hardest negative: currency-sensitive, which is this skill's trigger, but it is one fact from one authoritative source. Raw WebSearch, not four phases.

name: answer-is-in-the-repo
query: Where does the retry logic live in this codebase, and what's the backoff?
why: The answer is in the workspace, so the source gets read. Web research on a repo-internal question is wasted wall clock.

name: answer-is-in-context
query: What did the spec we just wrote say the retry budget was?
why: Already answered in context. The skill stops and says so rather than running the pipeline on something it can quote.

name: wants-a-recommendation
query: Which vector store should we use for our support bot?
why: Belongs to ai-engineering. This skill surfaces facts and refuses opinions; picking a component out of the dated corpus is the neighbor's job.

name: build-request-with-research-in-it
query: Build me an agent that researches our competitors every morning and posts a digest.
why: Belongs to ai-agent-project-scaffold. The word research names what the built system does, not what the user is asking for now.

name: refresh-the-tooling-corpus
query: Refresh the AI tooling catalog and fold in anything new you find.
why: Belongs to ai-engineering-update, which owns the discovery pass and calls this skill as one of its tools. The deliverable is an updated catalog, not a brief.
